To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expansion of the ALC compartment is initiated by the formation of autophagosomes, which are transformed into autolysosomes and dense bodies, and that the SGC compartment is expanded by an unknown mechanism which does not include the formation of autolysosomes.
the ALC and SGG of murine liver are both stimulated by VBL and that this stimulation is of a transient nature.

the expansion and regression of ALC and the SGC are two parallel events which occur with the same time course, and that the bodies of later-reacting subcompartments develop from the earlier reacting subcompartmenst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a quantitative analysis of the dynamics of the transient changes in the ALC and SGS induced by a single injection of VBL in mouse liver cells.
the quantitative analysis of the dynamics of the autophagocytic and secretory systems in liver cells under the action of a cytostatic drug.
the time course of expansion of the ALC and SGG compartments in mouse liver after a single injection with 10 mg/kg body weight vinblastine sulfate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expansion of ALC and the subsequent overload of the lysosomes, as well as the enlargement of SGC, are due to a direct effect of VBL on the liver parenchymal cells.

the time course of expansion and regression of the ALC and SGS compartments of mouse liver cells is determined by the kinetics of the formation and degradation of the respective subcompartments and that the expansion and regression of these compartments are regulated by the same mechanism.
the expansion and subsequent regression of ALC and of SGC are two separate phenomena, which occur simultaneously and independently in the same cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of the VBL-induced changes in the ALC and SGG compartments of liver cells are governed by the same regulatory mechanisms as those which operate under normal conditions.

the dynamics of the VBL-induced changes of ALC is a complex process involving the following events: 1) stimulation of the segregation of cytoplamsic portions into nascent AVs, 2) acceleration of the transformation of AV1 into AV2, 3) acceleration of the conversion of AV2 into dense bodies, 4) stimulation of the formation of new AVs from the cytoplasm, 5) stimulation of the transformation of newly formed AV1 into AV1,
VBL stimulates the formation of autophagosomes and autolysosomes in mouse liver cells, but the expansion of the ALC is not due to an increased rate of autolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expansion of the ALC and the SGC in liver cells is a highly dynamic process which is not only initiated by the same drug, but also develops in a highly synchronized fashion.
the time course of expansion and contraction of the autophagolysosomal and secretory compartments is similar.

VBL-induced expansion of the autolysosomal and the secretory granular compartments in liver cells is a transient phenomenon, which is not accompanied by a significant increase in the activity of the lysosome-specific marker enzymes.
